content.title: About
content.content: Cornbread stuffing is a traditional American side dish made from crumbled cornbread, vegetables, herbs, and sometimes meat. It is commonly served with turkey or chicken during holidays, adding a savory, slightly sweet flavor and a pleasant crumbly texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cornbread stuffing originated in the Southern United States, where corn is a staple crop.
The classic recipe includes the "holy trinity" of onion, celery, and carrot.
Some regional versions add sausage, bacon, or nuts for extra richness.
Baking the stuffing in a ceramic dish creates a golden, crispy crust.
Vegetarian versions omit meat and often incorporate mushrooms and nuts.

items.title: Source of whole grains
items.content: Cornbread provides whole‑grain carbohydrates and fiber that support healthy digestion.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains thiamine, niacin, and folate, which aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Corn supplies lutein and zeaxanthin, nutrients beneficial for eye health.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When prepared with minimal oil, the dish remains relatively low in saturated fats.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Vegetables like onion and carrot add vitamin C and beta‑carotene, boosting immune defenses.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to corn products, experiencing skin or digestive reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared stuffing often contains added salt; people with hypertension should monitor portions.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Cornbread can raise blood sugar quickly, so diabetics should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: High fiber levels may cause bloating in those with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the stuffing hot as a side to roasted poultry, beef, or vegetable mains. It can also be used as a filling for stuffed peppers or layered in casseroles. Fresh herbs such as sage or parsley enhance the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked stuffing in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before serving.
